description: Tonkotsu Ramen Pork Bone Broth is the heart and soul of a truly authentic Japanese ramen experience. This rich, milky white broth is slow-simmered to extract maximum flavor and collagen from pork bones, creating an incredibly deep and satisfying base. Its velvety texture and profound umami notes make it the perfect foundation for your favorite ramen toppings.

instructions.title: Prepare and Blanch Pork Bones
instructions.text: Thoroughly wash the pork femurs, knuckles, and trotters under cold running water. Place the bones in a large stockpot and cover with cold water. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat and continue boiling for 10 minutes to remove impurities. Skim off any scum that rises to the surface.

instructions.title: Clean Bones and Pot
instructions.text: Drain the blanched bones and rinse them very well under cold water, scrubbing off any remaining impurities or dark bits. Discard the blanched water. Clean the stockpot thoroughly to ensure no residue remains.

instructions.title: Start the Broth Simmer
instructions.text: Return the clean bones to the clean stockpot. Add 4 liters of fresh cold water, ensuring the bones are fully submerged. Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then immediately reduce the heat to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot and let it cook.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics
instructions.text: After the initial simmer, add the halved yellow onion, smashed garlic cloves, sliced fresh ginger, and green parts of scallions to the pot. Stir gently to combine. Continue to simmer the broth, partially covered, maintaining a gentle boil to encourage emulsification.

instructions.title: Emulsify and Adjust
instructions.text: Continue to simmer the broth. During this time, the broth should begin to turn milky white as the collagen and fat emulsify. Stir occasionally and ensure the water level is maintained by adding hot water if necessary to keep the bones submerged. This step is crucial for the signature Tonkotsu texture.

instructions.title: Strain and Season the Broth
instructions.text: Carefully remove the bones and aromatics from the pot using tongs or a slotted spoon. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a clean container, discarding any solids. Season the finished Tonkotsu broth with salt to taste. It is now ready to be used as the base for your ramen.

tips: For a truly milky broth, maintain a vigorous but gentle boil throughout the simmering process to emulsify the fats and collagen. Do not let it reduce too much.
Cracking the pork bones into smaller pieces before cooking helps extract more flavor and collagen, contributing to a richer broth.
Store cooled Tonkotsu broth in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days, or freeze for up to 2-3 months for longer storage.
